text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-The Conservatives took over the running of Oslo's City Council on Wednesday from the Labour Party. New council leader Fritz Huitfeldt did not present any plans, but said he was confident that left-wing parties would support budget plans.
-Norwegian explorer Boerge Ousland is about to end his expedition across Antarctica. Ousland will be the first person ever to cross Antarctica alone.
-Norwegian women earn 20 percent less than men. The wage gap between the sexes has been almost constant over the last 15 years.
-Den Norske Bank, Norway's largest commercial bank, expects interest rates to fall further. DnB estimates that money rates will fall to three percent in 1997.
-Oil companies are expected to invest 1,500 billion crowns in the Norwegian continental shelf over the next 25 years, 250 million crowns more than was spent in the last 25 years.
